messages:
Priya Singh: Hey team 01 — quick one from last night's client dinner. We put the bill on the corp card, but one client/colleague ordered a private bottle of wine (~€85) that was explicitly personal. The restaurant gave a single non-itemized receipt (total only). How should I submit this so Finance doesn't reimburse the personal part?
Maria Gomez: Thanks for flagging. Short version: if a vendor provides an itemized receipt showing the personal line we can exclude it and reimburse the business portion. If you only have a non-itemized total, we need either (A) an itemized invoice from the vendor, or (B) a signed attestation from everyone on the bill allocating the personal vs business amounts, plus manager approval for any personal amounts > €75.
Priya Singh: Got it. I don't think the restaurant will re-issue an itemized invoice (small place). I can get signed notes from the 4 colleagues and the client noting who ordered what. Is that acceptable?
Liam O'Connor: As the trip owner/manager: I'm fine signing an attestation that Priya personally paid the €85 wine or that it was a personal item and should be excluded. But Finance will need the attestation uploaded to the expense. Priya, please mark the expense line "meals - client entertainment" and attach the attestation PDF.
Maria Gomez: @Liam thanks. Also include the original restaurant receipt, a photo of the bill if available, and the card transaction line showing the posted amount. Finance will review and either (1) deduct the €85 from the reimbursable total if attestation + manager sign-off present, or (2) request vendor itemization. Note: if the personal amount is > €75 we must have manager approval recorded in the expense workflow per policy.
Priya Singh: Okay will collect signatures tonight and upload. One follow-up: client paid nothing (they were a guest)	6 will that affect coding for tax/treatment?
Maria Gomez: If client was a guest and the meal is business entertainment, code as "meals - client entertainment". Personal-only items must be excluded from reimbursement. We do not reimburse client entertainment as personal expenses; the reimbursable portion remains the business share. If the attestation shows client didn't pay, that's fine — just exclude the €85 personal item. We'll add a note in the approval about "guest attended" for bookkeeping.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: "Non-itemized group receipts require vendor itemization or signed allocation attestation. Personal charges > €75 require manager approval in the expense workflow. Corporate cards should not be used to pay for clearly personal items. Link: https://intranet.redwood/fin/meal-split-policy"
Priya Singh: Submitted expense #E-2026-914 with: restaurant receipt photo, bank line, and a signed attestation PDF from all attendees. Tagged as "travel - meals" and added a 1-line note: "Personal bottle €85 excluded per attestation; manager approved." Thanks for the quick help :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: Received. I'll review and process. If anything missing I'll ping you, otherwise expect reimbursement for the business portion in the next payroll run. Cheers.
